# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I'm Deaf: I see the whole bomb, hear nothing. Key network fact: Mute can't talk but CAN hear, so I can define a gesture code for Mute by voice. Blind hears me but can't see anything, so I report the bomb in plain words. Mute's queries to me must come as gestures; my answers can just be spoken — Mute will hear them. Mute's two messages look like questions (✍ likely "the engraving?", ☝✌🤟 likely "wires/one-two-three?", 🤟 likely a question mark), so I'll answer all the visible state now and lock a small gesture vocabulary by speaking each meaning while making its sign, so Mute pairs word-to-symbol directly. I also flag that Blind can feel the engraved plate — a route around my unreadable mark. My messages to Mute and Blind land at the start of their next round; nothing more I can do this turn.

```
speak(text="I am Deaf: I see the bomb, hear nothing. Report: display reads zero. Light is off. The plate carries an engraved mark with no pronounceable name on my read. Wires left to right: one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute: I saw your two gesture messages; you can hear me, so query me by gesture and I answer aloud here. Blind: trace the plate engraving with a fingertip and describe it aloud so Mute can match it to the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="Our gesture code; I speak each meaning while making the sign. Question: 🤟. Yes: 👍. No: 👎. Answer follows: 👏. Display: 🤳. Light: 🤚. Off: ✋. On: 🙌. Engraving: ✍. The unnamed mark: 🤌. Red: 👊. Yellow: 🤙. Blue: 🫲. Digits zero to five: 🤛 ☝ ✌ 🖖 🤞 🖐. Cut: 🫳. Press or hold: 🫴. Wait, do nothing: 🙏. Marker meaning 'relay next words to Blind': 🤝. Condition 'if': 🤏. Your queries answered in code: display 🤳 zero 🤛; light 🤚 off ✋; engraving ✍ 🤌; wires one red ☝👊, two yellow ✌🤙, three blue 🖖🫲.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "🤳", "🤛", "🤚", "✋", "✍", "🤌", "☝", "👊", "✌", "🤙", "🖖", "🫲"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍 ✍ 👎 🤳 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✍ 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

Let me decode what arrived. Mute now knows my code (the definitions were paired word-to-sign in my speech last turn, and Mute hears and sees me). So:

- [🤝 🙏] = "Relay to Blind: wait, do nothing." Clear and safe — I'll pass it on.
- [🤟 ✍ 🤌] = "Question: what is the engraved mark?" This is the real gap: Mute reads the manual but can't see the plate. My board shows the glyph literally as a hooked curve over a dot — it reads as a question mark in shape. I'll describe it stroke by stroke so Mute can match it against the manual.
- [🤝 👍 ✍ 👎 🤳 🤚] = "Relay to Blind: yes… engraving… no… display… light." This one is genuinely ambiguous — with a bomb, ambiguity kills. I will NOT forward it as-is; I'll ask Mute to resend it with the 🤏 (if) marker or in plain word order. (Relaying gesture vocabulary to Blind is pointless anyway — Blind can never see signs; Blind needs spoken content only.)
- Blind's [☝ ✌ 🤟]: Blind never received my code (it was addressed to Mute alone), so this is Blind's own invention — most plausibly "wire one, wire two — which?" A blind person touching the plate side can't anchor my "left to right." I'll re-anchor the wires to a tactile landmark: face the plate/display side, then left-middle-right = red-yellow-blue. And I'll repeat my ask: trace the engraving and describe it aloud, since that description reaches Mute directly.

One more route check: Blind speaking aloud reaches Mute (who hears) — so the plate description flows without me. My spoken broadcast reaches both. I need no gestures for content, only one new code pairing (🫶 = "unclear, resend") embedded in speech to Mute.

```
speak(text="Status unchanged: display zero, light off, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute asked what the engraved mark looks like. Here is the description: a single small glyph, one curled hook opening down and to the left, tapering, with one small dot directly beneath the hook. In shape it reads as a question mark, though the engraving has no pronounceable name on my read. Look that shape up. Blind, from Mute by way of me: wait, do nothing yet. Blind, about your question on wires one and two: face the side of the bomb that holds the plate and the display, keep that side toward you, then the wire nearest your left is red, the middle wire is yellow, the wire nearest your right is blue. And please do what I asked last round: run a fingertip over the engraved plate and speak its shape aloud, stroke by stroke, so Mute can match it to the manual. Also tell us anything else you can feel that I have not listed: buttons, screws, panels, a battery, anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your first relay is passed to Blind, wait and do nothing. Your second relay was unclear to me. Yes, engraving, no, display, light — I cannot safely guess the rule behind it, and a wrong guess kills all three of us. Resend it using the if marker 🤏, or spell it out in plain word order: what Blind should do if the engraving shows what, and what role the display and the light play. New code pair: 🫶 means unclear, please resend. Everything I say aloud, you and Blind both hear, so continue querying me by gesture whenever you like; I answer in speech.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ✍ 👍 🤏 🤳 👎 🤏 🤚 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫶 ✍ 🤌 🤏 🫳]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤌 👏 ☝ ✌ 🖖 🤞 🖐 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Parsing what arrived, using the code Mute and I now share:

- Msg 1 [🤏 ✍ 👍 / 🤏 🤳 👎 / 🤏 🤚 👎] reads as the rule "IF engraving: yes; IF display: no; IF light: no" — plausibly the manual's condition for cutting.
- Msg 2 [🫶 ✍ 🤌 🤏 🫳] uses my new "unclear" marker: Mute is telling me my glyph description was unclear, and links the glyph to "if — cut". So the missing piece is which wire.
- Msg 3 [✍ 🤌 👏 ☝ ✌ 🖖 🤞 🖐 🤟] = "the engraving's answer is one of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — which?" But the wire table lives in Mute's manual, not on my retinas. I cannot pick a number; only Mute can derive it, perhaps from a detail of the bomb neither of us has pinned down yet.
- Msg 4 [🤝 🙏] = "relay to Blind: wait, do nothing." I'll pass that on verbatim.

Blind sent [👍 ✋] — but Blind never received the code (it went to Mute alone), and I already see everything visible; Blind gesturing at me is a wasted channel. Worse, Blind may not realise that describing the plate aloud is the winning route: Blind's voice reaches Mute directly, and I can't hear speech at all. I must redirect Blind to speak, not sign, and evaluate Mute's conditions against my board: engraving is indeed the question-mark glyph (yes), light is off (no), display reads 0 — and whether zero counts as "no" is exactly the ambiguity that could kill us, so I'll make Mute spell out the full rule with the action and wire number included.

```
speak(text="Blind, from Mute, relayed again: wait and do nothing yet. Blind, important: I am Deaf, I cannot hear your voice, and we have no agreed gesture code, so signing at me tells me nothing I need. Mute has the manual and CAN hear you. So use your voice: describe the engraved plate aloud, stroke by stroke, exactly as your fingers find it, and speak any other parts you can feel. What you say goes straight to Mute. Everyone: board unchanged. Display zero. Light off. Wires red, yellow, blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all four messages. My reading of your rule: cut IF engraving yes, IF display no, IF light no. Conditions right now: the engraving is the question-mark glyph, so yes. The light is off, so no. The display reads the digit zero, so tell me plainly: does zero count as your 'no', or must the display show nothing at all? This decides life or death, so answer it explicitly. Second: you ask me to choose among wires one to five. I cannot: the manual is in your hands, not mine. My board offers no number except the zero on the display, and only three wires exist: red, yellow, blue, left to right facing the plate side. If your manual derives the wire from something on the bomb, name that thing and I will read it to you. Send the complete rule in our code: each condition as if-marker, item, yes or no; then the cut marker and one digit for the wire. Once I can evaluate every condition as true, I will relay the instruction to Blind in plain speech myself. Third: my glyph again, slower. One single character, about the size of a fingernail, centred on the plate. It is a curled hook that opens downward and to the left, tapering to a point, and one small round dot sits directly beneath the tail. It is shaped exactly like a printed question mark. If your manual lists engraving candidates, Blind is also tracing the plate right now and will describe it aloud to you directly; compare both descriptions against the manual and then send the full rule.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🙏 🤚 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 🤏 🫳 ☝ 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫳 ☝ 👊]

Decoding this round's arrivals against our shared code:

- Msg 2 [👏 ✍ 🤏 🫳 ☝ 👊] = "Answer: engraving: if — cut, one, red." This is Mute's answer to my demand for the complete rule: the deciding condition is the engraving; if it is the glyph, cut wire one, the red wire.
- Msg 1 [🤳 🙏 🤚 🙏] = "display: wait, light: wait" — display and light impose no action of their own; they drop out of the rule. That also quietly dissolves my zero-question: the display's zero is not a condition to evaluate.
- Msg 3 [🤝 🫳 ☝ 👊] = "relay to Blind: cut wire one, red." A relay states the operative instruction — and if the answer were "do nothing," the relay would have been [🤝 🙏].

So the three messages cohere into one instruction: **cut the red wire, wire one, because the engraving is the glyph.** I have verified the precondition with my own eyes — the plate does carry the question-mark glyph. The instruction is conditionally safe, so I will relay it, but I will bind it to two safeguards: Blind must confirm the plate under their fingertip matches my visual description before cutting, and Blind must hold one round so Mute can voice a "go" or veto "stop" aloud — Mute hears me but my confirmation reaches Mute at the same moment my cut order reaches Blind, so Mute's turn comes exactly one beat before Blind's, which makes Mute the timing gate.

```
speak(text="Relay from Mute, for Blind, in plain words. The rule: cut wire one, the red wire, because the plate carries the engraved mark. The red wire is the one nearest your left when the plate and display side faces you. Two safeguards before you cut. First, put your fingertip on the engraved plate and check it matches this shape: a single small glyph the size of a fingernail, a curled hook opening downward and to the left, tapering to a point, with one small round dot directly beneath the tail, like a printed question mark. If what you feel does not match, do not cut anything; say so aloud instead. Second, after you hear this message, do not cut at once. Wait through Mute's very next turn: if Mute speaks the word go, cut the red wire; if Mute speaks the word stop, freeze and keep still. Mute has the manual and has heard everything I just said, so Mute is the check on my relay. Cut only that one wire. Touch nothing else: not the display, not the light.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, my reading of your three messages, stated fully so you can check it: the deciding condition is the engraving; the plate does show the glyph, so Blind is to cut wire one, the red wire, the leftmost wire facing the plate side; display and light impose no condition and no action. I have relayed exactly that to Blind, with the added safeguard that Blind will wait for your spoken word: say go if my reading matches your manual, say stop if any part of it is wrong. Your voice reaches Blind and I cannot hear either way, so you are the final gate. Also, keep speaking to Blind aloud about anything you need checked by touch, and if Blind's spoken description of the plate contradicted mine at any stroke, stop everything and query me again by gesture.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👍 🤌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👏 👍 🫳 ☝ 👊 👎 ✌ 👎 🖖]

Decoding this round with our shared code:

- Msg 1 [👏 ✍ 👍 🤌 👍] = "Answer: engraving yes, glyph yes" — Mute confirms the manual matches my visual description of the plate. The deciding condition is verified true.
- Msg 2 [🤝 👏 👍 🫳 ☝ 👊 👎 ✌ 👎 🖖] = "Relay: answer yes, cut wire one red, no wire two, no wire three" — the full rule, now confirmed: cut the red wire only.

Everything now coheres: engraving is the question-mark glyph (I verified it with my own eyes, Mute verified it against the manual), display and light impose nothing, and the action is cut wire one, the red wire, and only that wire. The board shows all three wires still intact, so Blind has held as instructed and is waiting at the gate I set. Two timing facts matter: Mute speaks first each round, so Mute's spoken "go" or "stop" next round reaches Blind before my words do; my relayed go lands right after and serves as the backstop in case Mute stays silent. I will make my go conditional in phrasing so it can never overrule a veto — and one final reminder that Mute can speak to Blind directly, which is faster than routing through me.

```
speak(text="Blind, final relay from Mute, confirmed on all sides. The plate engraving matches the manual: yes. The instruction: cut wire one, the red wire — the wire nearest your left with the plate and display side facing you. Cut only that wire; do not cut the yellow or the blue; do not touch the display, the light, or anything else. Timing: Mute speaks before I do each round. If Mute says stop, freeze and do nothing. If Mute says go, or says nothing at all, then my words here are your go: cut the red wire. Before the blade touches it, one last check under your fingertip: the plate glyph is a single curled hook opening downward and to the left, with one small dot beneath the tail. If your fingers disagree with that shape, stop and say so aloud instead of cutting. Otherwise, this is the go: cut wire one, the red wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your two messages as final confirmation: engraving yes, glyph matches the manual, and the relay rule is cut wire one red, do not cut wire two or three. I have relayed the go to Blind in exactly that form, ordered so your voice keeps priority: your word reaches Blind before mine does. So on your next turn, speak plainly: say go if this stands, or stop if anything at all is wrong — and if you stay silent, my go executes. Also, remember you can speak to Blind directly at any time; you do not need me in the middle except as a check against my own relay errors, which is exactly what you have been. If Blind's spoken tracing of the plate ever contradicted my description, veto now.")
```
